reason: The passage demonstrates Yahweh's explicit goal to help and preserve the Hebrew people through multiple actions: (1) God's direct statement of preserving a faithful remnant of seven thousand in Israel who have not bowed to Baal ('וְהִשְׁאַרְתִּי בְיִשְׂרָאֵל שִׁבְעַת אֲלָפִים'), which shows intentional divine preservation; (2) Yahweh's appointment of new leadership—Hazael, Jehu, and Elisha—to restore proper governance and spiritual direction to the nation; (3) Divine sustenance provided through an angel who feeds Elijah during his wilderness journey, demonstrating God's care for His servant and by extension His people. These actions collectively establish that helping/preserving the Hebrew people is indeed one of Yahweh's stated objectives within this narrative.
